claim.text: Point Cloud Neural Networks contain sparse subnetworks obtained by magnitude-based pruning.
When only the top 1% of weights by magnitude are retained, the subnetworks described in claim 1 achieve test accuracies on the ModelNet40 dataset that are close to the unpruned baselines.
PointNet baseline 87.5% compared to 86.3% and 86.9%
DGCNN baseline 89.2% compared to 88.5% and 88.0%
PointCNN baseline 90.2% compared to 87.4% and 86.9%
Retaining only the top 1% highest-magnitude weights can preserve the majority of classification performance on ModelNet40 for the PCNN architectures, i.e., the Point Cloud Neural Networks.

Global magnitude pruning executed as a one-shot operation (a single pruning cycle, J=1) or as global Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP) identifies winning-ticket subnetworks at extreme sparsity levels on the ModelNet40 3D shape classification dataset more reliably than iterative layer-local pruning.

One-shot global pruning (a single pruning cycle, J=1) at 99% sparsity achieves higher test accuracy than both iterative local (i.e., layer-local) pruning and global Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP) across the PointNet, DGCNN, and PointCNN network architectures.
Sparse subnetworks discovered on the ShapeNetCore 3D dataset transfer to the ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN datasets while retaining comparable or acceptable accuracy after fine-tuning.
PointNet achieves 88.2% ( IMP) and 87.8% (one-shot global pruning) vs. dense baseline 87.5%;
DGCNN achieves 90.1% (IMP) and 90.4% (one-shot) vs. baseline 89.2%;
PointCNN achieves 90.6% (IMP) and 90.4% (one-shot) vs. baseline 90.2%.
PointNet achieves 71.7% (IMP) and 70.5% (one-shot) vs. baseline 68.2%;
DGCNN achieves 75.2% (IMP) and 74.9% (one-shot) vs. baseline 71.1%;
PointCNN achieves 73.2% (IMP) and 72.9% (one-shot) vs. baseline 70.4%.
At 99% sparsity, after fine-tuning, transferred accuracies on ModelNet40 remain close to dense baselines for sparse subnetworks discovered on the ShapeNetCore 3D dataset.
(PointNet IMP 86.3% vs. 87.5%)
(DGCNN IMP 88.5% vs. 89.2%)
(PointCNN IMP 87.4% vs. 90.2%)

At 99% sparsity, after fine-tuning, for sparse subnetworks discovered on the ShapeNetCore 3D dataset, the drops in transferred accuracies from dense baselines are larger on ScanObjectNN than on ModelNet40.
(PointNet IMP 64.7% vs. 68.2%)
(DGCNN IMP 64.6% vs. 71.1%)
(PointCNN IMP 65.3% vs. 70.4%)
Sparse subnetworks (winning tickets) discovered on one 3D domain can be reused to reduce training and parameter costs on related 3D classification tasks.
In Point Cloud Neural Networks (PCNNs), after magnitude pruning, convolutional layers retain a disproportionately large fraction of high-magnitude, task-critical weights.
In Point Cloud Neural Networks (PCNNs), after magnitude pruning, fully-connected (FC) layers contribute most of the removable parameters.
pruning only FC layer weights at a 99% pruning rate yields an overall network sparsity of 87% and a test accuracy of 88.3%
Pruning only convolutional layer weights at the same 99% rate yields an overall sparsity of only 12% and accuracy of 86.9%.
Simultaneously pruning both layer types to achieve 99% overall sparsity results in accuracy of 86.8% with 99% sparsity.
In Point Cloud Neural Networks (PCNNs), convolutional layers are the primary locus of critical weights for 3D feature extraction.
In Point Cloud Neural Networks (PCNNs), heavy pruning of fully-connected (FC) layers can dramatically reduce parameter count with limited or no loss in classification accuracy.

Subnetworks extracted from overparameterized Point Cloud Neural Networks (PCNNs) at extreme sparsity (99% pruning) yield models with parameter counts far below several compact, hand-designed 3D architectures while achieving competitive accuracy on the ModelNet40 dataset.
pruned PointNet has 0.034M parameters and 87.1% accuracy;
pruned DGCNN has 0.017M parameters and 86.3% accuracy;
pruned PointCNN has 0.012M parameters and 85.4% accuracy.
compact hand-designed models have 0.320M parameters
KCNet have 0.900M parameters.
Unstructured pruning of overparameterized Point Cloud Neural Networks (PCNNs) can produce extremely small models that are competitive with bespoke compact architectures.

Global magnitude pruning executed as a one-shot operation (a single pruning cycle, J=1) or as global Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP) identifies winning-ticket subnetworks at 99% sparsity on the ModelNet40 3D shape classification dataset more reliably than iterative layer-local pruning.
PointCNN has 0.320M parameters
